thread:
alex: Observed a 99th+ tail latency spike after flipping INT8 for KV cache on the fp8-preferring path. Started after yesterday's kernel selector tweak. Repro locally with single-stream long decode.

jordan: ugh. Same cluster? any correlation with batch size changes or adaptive batching? :thinking:

alex: Cluster-wide but only on models with >2k context. Baseline (FP8 KV) p99 ~= 45ms, with INT8 KV enabled some tails jump to 220-350ms intermittently. Avg unaffected. No change to batch target.

sara: do you have traces? can you paste a short profiler snapshot? might be KV page-eviction thrash or kernel fallback thrash.

alex: pasted quick pprof extract (top lines):
```
cpu_seconds: 120.4 total
  runtime.kernel_dispatch  58.3s
  kv_cache.decode_path     23.1s
  kv_cache.repack_pages    12.0s
  kernel.fp8_to_int8_conv  9.5s
  scheduler.wait_spin      7.2s
```

alex: Note the repack_pages bump aligns with tails. Looks like when INT8 KV active we do an occasional page compaction.

mike: could be fragmentation from smaller quantized slabs. Were we using the new slab allocator flag? `--kv-slab-compact=true` rolled out last week.

alex: yes that flag. Rolling back locally removes the big tail. But leaving it off globally increases memory by ~8%.

sara: For quality regression: any decode mismatches? INT8 KV might introduce slight logits noise if calibration off.

alex: small sample diff from stream compare (gold vs int8-kv):
```
gold: "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog."
int8-kv: "The quick brown fox jumps over a lazy dog ."
logit-delta mean ~0.02 across tokens, spike at token 8=0.12
```

jordan: that delta seems within expected but the timing spike is worse. Could be garbage collection inside repack or a slow kernel path triggered for certain sequence lengths. Any kernel switch logs?

alex: kernel switch log snippet when spike happened:
```
[12:03:21] selected kernel fp8_matmul_fast
[12:03:21] switched to int8_kv_unpack (fallback path)
[12:03:21] repack_pages start
[12:03:21] repack_pages end (120ms)
```

sara: repack_pages being 120ms explains p99. Need to avoid synchronous compaction during active decode. We can change compaction to async or add hysteresis so compaction only runs when idle for N ms.

mike: agree. Also consider widening the slab size for INT8 lanes to reduce fragmentation. Quick experiment: set `kv-slab-size=2MB` and `kv-slab-compact-threshold=0.6`.

alex: trying that now on a staging replica. Also going to add a kernel_selector guard so we avoid switching to the slower unpack path mid-decode.

deploy-bot: deploy 2245008012 by alex to staging started (sha: d4f7c2).

jordan: once you have staging numbers, post p99 and memory delta. If compaction async reduces tail but memory rises <12% sounds acceptable for now.

alex: staging run results after changes: p99 went from 260ms -> 52ms, avg unchanged. Memory +10%. Quality diffs identical to earlier small token shifts. Will open a small RFC to: 1) make compaction async w/ idle hysteresis, 2) add slab size tuning defaults for INT8 KV, 3) guard kernel switch mid-decode.

sara: sounds good. add a unit test to simulate long single-stream decode forcing compaction to ensure async works.

mike: also add a perf test to periodically run 1k single-stream decodes and assert p99 < 80ms.

alex: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
